title: Power Pages: MCP server exposes site data to AI clients
summary: Hold: the governance paths do not match their linked instructions, including a missing Products section in the public-access policy path. The statement that agents can query anything allowed by table permissions overlooks Web API exposure and column restrictions; claims about arbitrary queries and misconfiguration exposing the endpoint also need narrowing.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide switch specifically for Power Pages MCP server is documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP server tenant admin disable; Power Pages MCP tenant-wide disable PowerShell API. Opened mcp-overview, mcp-configure-site-settings and copilot-hub. Found per-site MCP/Enabled; no tenant-wide Power Pages MCP-server switch.

claims.claim: Agents can query anything the signed-in user's web role and table permissions allow.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose. ... You can configure column permissions to further define privileges to individual columns within a table while using the portal Web API.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'Agent access through the site's Web API respects web roles and table permissions, and is also limited by the tables and columns exposed through the Web API and any column permissions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/web-api-overview.

claims.claim: An agent can issue arbitrary queries against the site.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP arbitrary queries; Power Pages MCP Web API table permissions queries authentication misconfigured. Opened mcp-overview and web-api-overview. They document conversational CRUD through a constrained Web API, not arbitrary query execution.
claims.fix: Replace 'Table permissions that were adequate for a form-based site can behave differently when an agent issues arbitrary queries.' with 'Review existing table permissions before exposing site data through natural-language queries.'

claims.claim: Misconfigured authentication site settings can break sign-in.
claims.quote: Configure authentication providers, validate authentication settings, and diagnose common sign-in problems. ... Users click Sign in but return to the sign-in page. Help me identify the problem.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/security-agent#security-scenarios for the sign-in troubleshooting statement, or narrow it to the MCP configuration article's statement that incorrect site-setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly.

claims.claim: Misconfigured site settings can leave the MCP endpoint exposed.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP misconfigured authentication endpoint exposed. Opened mcp-configure-site-settings and mcp-overview; read security-agent search excerpts. No passage states that an MCP site-setting error bypasses authentication or exposes the endpoint.
claims.fix: Remove 'or leave the endpoint exposed'. Alternatively replace the entire bullet with 'Incorrect site-setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/mcp-configure-site-settings#verify-configuration.
